claim: The Stresa-Alpino-Mottarone cable car has remained closed since the 23 May 2021 disaster in which the traction cable snapped near the summit, killing 14 people.
quote: the traction or haulage cable snapped about 5 metres (16 ft) from the summit... it has remained closed ever since

claim: Stresa's official tourism office confirms the cablecar remains closed with no announced reopening; tourist office hours run through November 2026.
The cable car operator and engineers admitted to blocking emergency brakes to avoid downtime, which became routine practice prior to the disaster.
quote: blocking the emergency brakes had become common practice to avoid downtime when brakes were malfunctioning

claim: Alpyland alpine coaster operates 10:00-17:00 weekdays and 10:00-18:00 weekends; single full ride €6.50, single reduced ride €5.50, with multi-ride packages up to 10 trips.
Alpyland requires riders to be at least 4 years old and 100 cm tall; the two-seat bobsleds have rider-adjustable speed.
quote: All children aged 4 and above, with a minimum height of 100 cm, can ride

claim: Giardino Botanico Alpinia is open daily 9:30-18:00 weather permitting, with full admission €5.00 and reduced €4.50 for children 4-12 or groups.
quote: dalle 9.30 alle 18.00 TUTTI I GIORNI, FESTIVI INCLUSI

claim: Giardino Botanico Alpinia sits at roughly 800 m altitude above Stresa and specializes in alpine flora.
quote: alpine plants, located at 800 meters altitude above Stresa on Lake Maggiore

claim: From Mottarone's 1,491 m summit, seven lakes are visible: Orta, Maggiore, Mergozzo, Comabbio, Monate, Varese and Biandronno.
quote: From Mottarone's top you can see 7 different lakes: Orta, Maggiore, Mergozzo, Comabbio, Monate, Varese and Biandronno

claim: The Parco del Mottarone summit (1,492 m) offers a 360° panorama and over 15 km of ski slopes in winter, plus the Rifugio Genziana refuge restaurant.
quote: seven shimmering lakes: Maggiore, Orta, Mergozzo, Varese, Comabbio, Monate, and Biandronno

claim: The summit panorama spans from the Ligurian Apennines and Maritime Alps to Monte Rosa, Monviso, and the Swiss high peaks across the Po Plain.
quote: uninterrupted 360° panorama from the Ligurian Apennines and the Maritime Alps to the Monte Rosa massif, the Monviso and the high peaks of Switzerland

claim: The Mottarone MTB area has an extensive trail network with maintained singletrack across difficulty grades; the Mottarone Trail Park has about ten routes starting from Bar Stazione near Alpino with on-site bike rental.
quote: Mottarone Trail Park offers about ten maintained single-track routes of varying difficulty, all starting and ending at the Bar Stazione near Alpino

claim: Mottarone is accessible by road from Armeno on the Lake Orta side (the 'Due Riviere') or by the private Borromea toll road from Stresa-Gignese.
quote: the 'Due Riviere' road from Armeno, or the private 'Borromea' road (toll) from Stresa-Gignese

claim: The Borromea private toll road from Alpino costs €10 for cars and €7 for motorbikes, while the Armeno road from Lake Orta is free of charge.
quote: The fee for the private Borromea toll road is €10 for cars and €7 for motorbikes

claim: Villa Crespi's own magazine highlights Mottarone for its seven-lake panorama, hiking through pine-fir-beech-larch-chestnut forests, and winter ski runs.
quote: the natural splendor of the 'Seven Lakes'... Orta, Maggiore, Mergozzo, Biandronno, Varese, Monate, and Comabbio

claim: Mottarone is roughly a half-hour winding drive from Orta via Armeno, with the route considered the natural mountain backdrop to Lake Orta.
quote: Mottarone is one of the lowest peaks of all the Alps, but reserves to the visitors one of the most beautiful landescape
